study.title: IMAGING OF BRAIN FUNCTION BASED ON THE ANALYSIS OF FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY - IMAGING ANALYSIS OF BRAIN FUNCTION BY FMRI AFTER ACUPUNCTURE AT LR3 IN HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS
study.journal: Afr J Tradit Complement Altern Med.
study.study_design: randomized, before-after study design with three parallel groups
study.blinding: volunteers' eyes were masked with eyeshades, and earplugs were simultaneously worn; blinding of participants to acupoint type implied but not explicitly described for assessors
study.population: healthy subjects randomly selected from universities and colleges in Guangzhou city, China
study.inclusion_criteria: age between 21 and 28 years; right handedness; regular diet with minimal liquor, tobacco, tea, and coffee consumption; normal sleeping patterns (before 12 a.m.); moderate-sized body mass index of 18.5–23.9 (Chinese); no history of nervous system disease; no pain (including dysmenorrheal) or insomnia within 1 month before the test; no metallic substances in the body, such as stents; no noise exposure and hypothermia; no fear of confined spaces; no acupuncture procedure within 1 month before the test
study.exclusion_criteria: did not meet inclusion criteria (implied from flowchart); refused to participate

interventions.procedure_label_exact: True acupuncture at the LR3 acupoint
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: On the dorsum of the foot, in the depression anterior to the junction of the first and second metatarsal bones (Chinese National Standards GB/T12346)
interventions.manipulation_exact: tube needling technique; needle handle tapped softly using a forefinger; after developing needle sensation, twirling at an angle of 90–180° and a frequency of 60–90 times/min and lifting and thrusting at a range of 0.3–0.5 cm and a frequency of 60–90 times/min were conducted; after manipulating the needle for 1 min, the needle was held in place for 30 min; during the 30 min, the physician repeated this manipulation for 1 min every 10 min
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects were asked to pass urine and stool prior to treatment; eyes masked with eyeshades; earplugs worn
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: to validate the acupoint specificity of LR3

extraction_notes.note: Sensory/deqi assessment: The paper does not report any formal deqi or sensory questionnaire (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) results. Deqi is only mentioned as 'needle sensation' in the context of needle manipulation. No quantitative data on deqi are provided.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. No instrument, data, or narrative regarding these constructs was found in the paper.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the paper.

Detailed fMRI acquisition parameters (TR, TE, voxel size, flip angle, number of slices) are referenced to 'our previous study (Wu C, et al., 2014)' and are not reproduced in this paper. These could not be extracted from the present document.
ReHo analysis parameters are also referenced to 'our previous study (Wu C, et al., 2014)' and are not reproduced in this paper.
The paper states that 90 subjects were screened, 74 met inclusion criteria, 45 agreed to participate and were randomized. However, the reason 29 of the 74 eligible subjects refused is not clarified.
extraction_notes.source_location: Figure 1 (Flowchart), page 92; Methods/General Data section, page 91

extraction_notes.note: The direction of the functional connectivity changes (all negative peak intensities in contrast_01 and contrast_02, all positive in contrast_03) is reported in the tables. The legend states 'positive numbers (colors) represent activation, negative numbers (colors) represent deactivation.' However, in the context of seed-based functional connectivity analysis, the sign of the t-statistic reflects the direction of the between-condition difference (e.g., less connectivity after acupuncture vs. before), not necessarily deactivation per se. This should be interpreted with caution.
extraction_notes.source_location: Figure 4, 5, 6 captions and color bar legends, pages 95-97

extraction_notes.note: The contrast for 'before vs. after acupuncture at LR3' (Table 2) is described as a within-group pre vs. post comparison for the LR3 arm only. The n analyzed for this contrast is inferred to be 15 based on group size; it is not explicitly stated.

The ROI seed point is described as 'the center of a sphere with a radius of 1 mm' which is an unusually small radius for a seed ROI in fMRI. This may reflect a single voxel or may be a reporting error. Preserved as reported.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods/ROI Identification section, page 94; Methods/fMRI Analyses section, page 94

extraction_notes.note: The paper performs ALFF, ReHo, and functional connectivity analyses, but the main results reported here are the functional connectivity findings. ALFF and ReHo results themselves (beyond identification of the seed) are not reported in detail in this paper and are described as previously published (Wu C, et al., 2014).
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods/ReHo Analysis and ROI Identification sections, page 94

extraction_notes.note: The n_analyzed values for between-group contrasts (contrast_02: true vs. sham acupuncture; contrast_03: LR3 vs. sham acupoint) are inferred as 30 (15 per group × 2 groups) based on group sizes. This is not explicitly stated for each contrast in the results section.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were reported. The study focused solely on neuroimaging outcomes.

Brodmann area labels in Tables 2–4: most clusters show '-' under BA column, indicating Brodmann area was not assigned. Only cluster 3 in Table 2 (Inferior Temporal Gyrus) has BA 37 assigned. This has been preserved exactly as reported.

The paper does not explicitly state whether the t-tests used for the three contrasts are paired or unpaired. The before vs. after contrast within the LR3 group would be expected to use a paired t-test, while the between-group comparisons would use unpaired t-tests, but this is not explicitly stated.
